clue.text: Close a valve thus, perhaps

parts.note: closing a valve stops a flow, and the word for the closing action itself is a stopping mechanism

explanation.surface: An instruction for an engineer about how to close a valve.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap or valve that stops a supply is the device that closes it, so closing a valve is exactly this action.

clue.text: Con man turns up in disgrace

parts.note: to con a text is to study or scan it

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the word for man is read bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A trickster reappears amid public shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is an outrage causing public shame.

clue.text: Discover a foreign planet

parts.note: un is French for a
Earth is our planet

explanation.surface: Astronomers find an alien world.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up or bring it to light.

clue.text: Scotch governor?

parts.note: not a Scottish ruler but the bar device that regulates measures of whisky poured from an upturned bottle

explanation.definitionFit: A pub dispenser fixed to a spirit bottle controls each measure served, governing the whisky.

clue.text: Boxer of cunning and power

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or crafty
weight means influence or power

explanation.surface: A fighter known for guile and strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer in the lightest professional weight division is named after this class.

clue.text: Meals for father in breaks from work

indicators.note: the word for father sits inside the word for breaks

parts.note: rests are pauses from work
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad's meals are taken during his work breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal.

clue.text: To do so the wrong way will go against the grain

definitions.text: To do so the wrong way will go against the grain

parts.words: To do so the wrong way will go against the grain
parts.note: stroking or polishing something in the wrong direction against its grain refers to the idiom about irritating someone

explanation.definitionFit: To polish or massage something; doing it the wrong way is the idiom for irritating a person.

clue.text: A driver going round in circles

definitions.text: A driver going round in circles

parts.words: A driver going round in circles
parts.note: not a lost motorist but a rotating screw that drives a ship or plane forward

explanation.definitionFit: This rotating bladed device drives a vessel or aircraft by spinning.

clue.text: A couple of scraps for bird

parts.note: a spar is a sparring bout, a minor fight
a row is a quarrel, another kind of scrap

explanation.surface: A bird picks up two bits of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scraps' are fights, not leftovers: two words for a scrap are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A common small brown songbird.

clue.text: Yet it's a misplaced feeling of gratification

indicators.note: misplaced says the letters of yet it's a are put in the wrong places

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's sense of satisfaction is unwarranted.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiety is the state of being fully satisfied, as after eating.

clue.text: Play Ted reviewed with expertise

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters of play ted are looked at again and set out afresh

explanation.surface: A critic reviews a play by someone called Ted, writing knowledgeably.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something skilfully, like an expert, is doing it with expertise.

clue.text: Cheerful boy and aunt played together

indicators.note: played here means the letters of boy and aunt are toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A happy boy and his aunt enjoy a game together.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyant in mood means light-hearted and optimistic.

clue.text: Most inexpensive hat priced wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly signals that the letters of hat priced are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A shop has mispriced a hat at the bargain end of the range.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely cheap is the least costly option, as in the idiom.

clue.text: Strange how mill-race ends in the lake

indicators.note: ends picks out the final letter of the word mill-race

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the odd way a mill stream flows out into a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie describes something weird and unsettling.

clue.text: Hard-hearted king whose widow was merry

indicators.note: hearted says a letter is placed at the heart of the king's name

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A cruel monarch whose widow, oddly, was cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehár composed the operetta The Merry Widow, so the 'widow' is his work, not a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer wrote The Merry Widow, the operetta whose title character is a cheerful rich widow.

clue.text: He's not left with support in defence

definitions.text: He's not left with support in defence

parts.note: the opposite of left is right
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A football defender on one flank, backing up his team.
explanation.walkthrough: A football position: the defender on the right-hand side of the back line.
explanation.definitionFit: In football this is a defender playing on the right flank, so the whole clue describes his role.

clue.text: Move to the middle 'and compromise

definitions.meaning: travel only to the halfway point
meet someone partway in an agreement

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch speaker urges someone to shift centrewards and meet them partway.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally covering half a distance, and figuratively conceding half the ground in a negotiation.

clue.text: Upholstery material that is harsh or rough

indicators.note: rough suggests the letters are roughed up and jumbled

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A fabric for chairs that feels coarse and scratchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff fibre from a horse's mane or tail was traditionally used to stuff furniture.

clue.text: Reptile giving a girl a lot of trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of a girl a lot are stirred up and disordered

explanation.surface: A reptile causes a young woman a lot of bother.
explanation.definitionFit: The alligator is a large crocodilian reptile.

clue.text: Not a sum that's incorrect — sums

indicators.note: incorrect says the letters of not a sum are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A teacher marks some additions as wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Totals or quantities of money are amounts.

clue.text: Heir took in, in wild glee

indicators.note: the second in places the eating word within the scrambled glee
wild means the letters of glee are thrown into disorder

parts.note: ate means consumed, took in as food

explanation.surface: An heir swallows the news with wild delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took in' looks like part of the container signal, but it is the eating word; the second 'in' does the placing, while 'wild' scrambles the glee.
explanation.definitionFit: A person bequeathed something in a will receives a legacy.

clue.text: Italian capital has nothing for Juliet's husband

parts.note: Rome is the capital city of Italy
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A statement about the Italian capital lacking something, set beside Shakespeare's lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play the young lovers marry secretly, so he is her husband.

clue.text: She makes personal deliveries

parts.note: not a courier but a woman who helps deliver babies

explanation.definitionFit: A nurse trained to assist at childbirth delivers babies by hand.

clue.text: Arranged, but not voluntary

definitions.meaning: commanded, done because one was told to

explanation.definitionFit: Both set out in sequence and commanded by authority, hence compulsory rather than freely chosen.

clue.text: Have a duty, even if it might be tough?

indicators.note: might be hints that the word tough could become another word if its letters were reordered

explanation.surface: A grumble that an obligation may prove hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: This modal verb expresses obligation, as in being bound to do something.

clue.text: Such a discussion gives chance for falling out

definitions.text: Such a discussion gives chance for falling out

parts.words: Such a discussion gives chance for falling out
parts.note: a debate with no fixed conclusion leaves room for disagreement, and its closing stage is left unsealed so things may spill out

explanation.surface: A remark that an unstructured debate risks people quarrelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate without a set limit or conclusion is unrestricted, leaving room for argument.

clue.text: Shows fond regard for the opposite sex

definitions.text: Shows fond regard for the opposite sex

parts.words: Shows fond regard for the opposite sex
parts.note: regard is taken literally as looking: eyeing up admiringly

explanation.definitionFit: To leer or eye someone amorously is to look at them with desire.

clue.text: Build straight up

explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for constructing a building and an adjective for standing upright.

clue.text: Girl holds bat incorrectly in game

indicators.note: holds means the girl's name wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Nell is a girl's name

indicators.note: incorrectly says the letters of bat are wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: A girl grips her bat the wrong way during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' turns BAT into TBA, which NELL holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team ball sport played mostly by women, popular in Britain and the Commonwealth.

clue.text: Studio that is later converted

indicators.note: converted implies the letters are changed into a new form

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: An announcement that a studio will be renovated later.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or designer's workshop is called by this French word.

clue.text: Arab leaders trembling in speech

indicators.note: in speech signals that a word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: shakes are fits of trembling

explanation.surface: Arab rulers nervously trembling as they deliver an address.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheikhs are chiefs or heads of Arab tribes, families or states.

clue.text: Arrested missing Pole perhaps, recovered tyre

indicators.note: perhaps hints the remaining letters might form another word in a different order
missing means a letter is dropped from arrested

parts.note: S stands for south, one of the earth's poles

explanation.surface: A man arrested without a Polish companion has a retreaded tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops S from ARRESTED to leave ARRETED, which 'perhaps' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre given a new tread is remoulded and reused, so it has a new covering.
